sentenceSets.sentence: The refulgent quality of the early enthusiasm made the subsequent dimming feel sharper than it would otherwise have seemed.

answerChoices.reasoning: Close, but the sentence sets up a contrast with a later 'dimming', which calls for a word naming enthusiasm at its most blazing rather than merely giving off soft light.
This carries a suggestion of heat and even fury, whereas the sentence tracks brightness alone as the thing that later faded.
Dazzling describes the effect on an observer whose eyes are overwhelmed, but the sentence attributes the quality to the enthusiasm itself as something that later dimmed.
A glow is low and steady, too faint a starting point to make the later dimming feel sharp by comparison.
Fervor names intensity of feeling, but the sentence uses a light metaphor throughout, pairing this quality with a 'dimming' rather than a cooling.
Buoyancy describes lightness of spirit, which does not set up the brightness-to-darkness contrast the second half of the sentence depends on.
Mere visibility would not make its loss feel sharp; the sentence implies something notably brilliant was lost.
Heady suggests intoxicating excitement, but the sentence's contrast is with dimming, not with sobering up.
Something already clouded could not later be described as dimming.
Lukewarm enthusiasm would make its decline unremarkable rather than sharp.
Sullenness contradicts the enthusiasm the sentence says was present at the start.

sentenceSets.sentence: At dusk the cathedral's west window turned refulgent, throwing panels of colored light across the worn stone floor.

answerChoices.reasoning: A gleam is reflected off a surface, but the window here is casting light onto the floor rather than catching a glint.
Blazing implies fire or fierce heat, which does not fit glass at dusk gently laying panels of color on the stone.
Iridescence involves colors shifting as the viewer moves, while the sentence describes steady panels of light thrown in one direction.
Luminescence means emitting light without heat from an internal source, but the window is lit from behind by the setting sun.
The light is explicitly described as colored, which rules out a single-hue description.
Vividness applies to the colors themselves and misses the brightness that lets the window project onto the floor.
Transparency is a permanent property of glass and could not be something the window 'turned' at dusk.
This would describe splitting light into a spectrum, whereas the colors here come from the stained panels themselves.
A window that blocked light could not throw colored panels across the floor.
Dullness contradicts the colored light filling the interior.
Physical damage has nothing to do with the transformation the sentence attributes to the fading daylight.

sentenceSets.sentence: Her refulgent stage presence made the rest of the cast seem to recede into the scenery whenever she entered.

answerChoices.reasoning: Radiance often suggests warmth or health beaming outward, while the sentence measures her presence by how thoroughly it outshines everyone else onstage.
This word points to sparkling wit and quickness, but the sentence says nothing about what she says, only about the effect of her entrance.
In describing a performer, 'brilliant' would be read as praise for skill, whereas the sentence describes an overwhelming visual presence that dims the other actors.
Coruscation implies flashing and glittering in bursts, at odds with a presence that steadily blots out the rest of the cast for as long as she is onstage.
Charisma is about drawing people toward you, but the sentence describes a light-and-shadow effect in which others visually fade away.
A commanding presence directs attention through authority, while the sentence has the other performers dissolving into the scenery rather than deferring to her.
Imposing suggests intimidating scale or bearing, and nothing in the sentence indicates the cast is cowed rather than eclipsed.
Arresting means it stops you short, yet the sentence emphasizes sustained brightness across her whole time onstage.
Someone modest and easily overlooked would not make an entire cast recede.
A stiff, lifeless performer is the opposite of one who dominates every scene she enters.
A subdued presence cannot be what pushes the other actors into the background.
